newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lloyd's offers strike insurance in Germany.
newsitem.headline: Lloyd's offers strike insurance in Germany.

text.p: A new insurance for German companies providing cover against the consequences of strikes at suppliers has been introduced by brokers Jaspers Industrie Assekuranz (JIA). Cover is provided by Lloyd's of London, JIA manager Johann Hendrik Mohr said on Wednesday in Duesseldorf.

German insurers already offer cover against loss-of-profit (business interruption) due to supply problems. Industrial companies have to take out fire LOP cover with extended coverage. However, the policy is limited to events caused by insured losses at the supplier's plant, said Mohr.
"If there is a fire at a supplier's plant and this causes the hold-up of parts, you are covered under this policy," he said.

However, if there was only a strike without any loss event, this cover would not be triggered, and this is where the new policy comes in. Insured sums go up to between 20 million and 30 million marks. An industrial customer has to name all suppliers to be covered, Mohr said.

Usually a deductible is agreed, equalling the losses from the first three days of the interruption. Mohr was not prepared to comment on prices for the cover. It had not been offered in Germany before, but had had some success in the UK and in France, he said.
